question: with several slots, does one running conversation cost what it costs on a single slot, and why did the server stall for 6-10 s when it saved a conversation
setup: 0.1.9 build against the build of this round, production profile with parallel 1 or 4, MTP off unless stated, no disk tier unless stated; tmp/pool_probe.py puts 50163 + 18939 + 1285 tokens of idle conversations in slots 1-3, then decodes 256 greedy tokens on a 23052-token conversation in slot 0

what_was_wrong.the pool: with more than one slot the cache is unified: every conversation sits in one pool of cells and each graph spans the pool (n_kv = the highest used cell). The sparse-attention block list of a batch held every conversation's blocks: their keys were gathered (12 x GET_ROWS [128, 23424] against [128, 5888] on one slot, 1.4 ms), scored and enumerated on the host (inputs 1.98 against 1.14 ms a step), only to be marked invisible
what_was_wrong.the stall: saving a slot's state read it from the device one cell range at a time. A conversation decoded alongside others is interleaved with them cell by cell, so it is thousands of ranges per layer; the user's log had gathers of 6255-10315 ms, during which the other conversations produced one token in 9 s

decode.MTP off: 0.1.9 47.6 ms/token (21.0 tok/s) -> 44.8-45.3 (22.1-22.3); one slot alone 44.1 (43.0 on 0.1.9); host inputs 1.98 -> 1.31 ms a step (one slot 1.14)
decode.MTP on: per speculative pass 88.9 -> 85.1 ms (one slot 81.0), 23.4 -> 25.5 tok/s at the same ~43% acceptance
decode.output: the 256 tokens and every top-3 probability identical to 0.1.9, with and without idle conversations resident; the 18.6K equivalence probe on one slot identical to 0.1.8

prefill.beside idle conversations: an 18939-token prefill beside a 50K one: 999 -> 1064-1069 t/s; four 43K conversations prefilled one after the other: 913 / 837 / 763 / 704 -> 903 / 893 / 835 / 877 t/s (the score bounds now apply beside other conversations too)

short_conversations.what changes: a conversation with fewer visible blocks than the selection budget (512 blocks, ~2K tokens) fills the budget with invisible entries; they now sit after its own blocks instead of among them, so its attention can differ in the last bits
short_conversations.measured: a 1527-token conversation beside the idle ones, first generated token: 0.1.9 ('``' -0.620, '</' -0.896), this round ('</' -0.716, '``' -0.767), the same conversation alone on one slot ('</' -0.680, '``' -0.806); LLAMA_QSA_ACTIVE_BLOCKS=0 reproduces 0.1.9 exactly. The new numbers no longer depend on which other conversations happen to be in the pool.

mixed_steps: several conversations decoding at once (tmp/mstream_agree_probe.py, 4 x 43K): every greedy token identical; the probabilities of a mixed step moved, but they move between two runs of the same build too - which requests land in which batch changes from run to run
